ABOUT THIS MODEL

Kollam district, from its Arabian Sea coast and Ashtamudi backwaters to the Western Ghats. The renderer, typography, glass panels, camera perspective and lighting follow the original Kozhikode 3D project.

Building footprints cover the mapped district boundary. Terrain, imagery, roads and water extend across the surrounding landscape. Zoom in for buildings and trees; use Whole district for the wider view.

Kerala & South India

Use Explore farther to open Kerala or South India. These regional views stream satellite imagery, terrain, roads, place names and mapped 3D buildings as you move. Jump to all 14 Kerala districts or major cities across the peninsula. Building coverage and height accuracy vary. The detailed Kollam model, tours, wards and healthcare directory remain available through Kollam.

Regional Kerala district outlines are the same 2021 Open Data Kerala / OpenStreetMap snapshot, simplified for display. Regional map data comes from OpenFreeMap / OpenMapTiles / OpenStreetMap, rendered with MapLibre GL JS. Satellite imagery remains Sentinel-2 cloudless 2020, EOX. Terrain is Mapzen / AWS. Regional map sources require an internet connection.

of buildings have mapped heights or floor counts. Others are plausible estimates, not measurements. Map coverage can contain omissions.

From geographic data

  • Building footprints, roads, rail and water: Overture Maps, 2026-10-21.0
  • Elevation: Mapzen / AWS Terrarium terrain tiles
  • Ground imagery: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2020, EOX
  • district boundary from Open Data Kerala / OpenStreetMap (2021 snapshot), for visualization, not legal or survey use

Generated details

  • Unmapped building heights, roofs, facade colors and night windows
  • trees and palms scattered using satellite greenery
  • Animated water shading and decorative street-light glow
  • Stylised Thangassery Lighthouse and Punalur bridge, with approximate dimensions and placement
  • Sun position for Kollam on an illustrative 15 January

Limits

This is a visual model, not traffic or flood prediction. Viewpoint pins locate areas, not entrances. The Jatayu sculpture and Palaruvi waterfall are not modelled. Imagery is historical and becomes soft at street level. The tour lines connect viewpoints and are not navigable road routes.
